_expect.name: Peyote Cracks Formation - E. Face (aka Bachar Toprope Wall)

ca_peyote_cracks_formation_e_face_aka_ba.blurb: The overhanging east side of the Peyote Cracks formation, in the Hidden Valley part of the Outback in Joshua Tree National Park. Ten climbs, nearly all of them hard: mostly 5.12 with a handful of 5.11 and 5.13 lines and one 5.14. Most are trad or toprope problems, with a couple of bolted leads. Several began life as toprope problems and were later turned into lead routes, which is why many parties still rope up from above. The wall is steep from end to end and short, so expect power and technique over endurance. It suits strong climbers only; there is little here for beginners.
ca_peyote_cracks_formation_e_face_aka_ba.approach: Two ways in. From the back loop of Hidden Valley Campground, head roughly north in the direction of Echo Cove; the formation sits about halfway along. Or leave the car at Echo Cove, follow the old road southwest, then take the climber trail that branches right to the rock.

ca_lower_wall.blurb: The first wall you meet on the walk in to the 4:20 Wall, in Rock Creek above Mammoth Lakes in the Eastern Sierra, at roughly 9,100 feet. It is a sub-vertical granite face that looks southeast, with ten climbs that mix trad and a few bolted lines. Grades run from the easy 5.7s through the 5.9s, with 5.10 the most common level and a single 5.11. A good pick for climbers working through moderates at a quiet, high-elevation spot, and the neighboring Higher Wall sits directly above for more options.

ca_mars.blurb: A small cliff in the Echo Rock area of Joshua Tree National Park, in front of the southwest side of Little Hunk. Ten easy-to-moderate climbs, almost all toprope with a pair of trad lines, running from the low 5th class through the 5.8 and 5.9 range with a single 5.10. The side facing the trail is sunny and sheltered in winter, while the smaller broken side opposite is shady. It is a short flat walk from the Echo Tee parking lot, which makes it a handy spot for beginners, new leaders or a quick toprope session.

ca_phantom_cart_the.blurb: A big lone boulder on a hillside in the Outer Rim of the Quail Springs bouldering zone in Joshua Tree National Park, roughly a mile walk from the road. It is really two blocks that split apart, and the gap between them forms a chimney that serves as the easy way up and down. Ten problems from very easy up to V5, with a mix of moderates and a couple of hard, fingery lines. The east side warms quickly in the morning, so early or late visits are more comfortable. Bring a couple of pads for the landings.

ca_pig_sty_the.blurb: A small cluster of odd-shaped boulders next door to the Manx Boulders, in the Hidden Valley area of Joshua Tree National Park. Ten problems with a wide spread: several very easy ones, a few in the V0 to V2 range, and a couple of much harder lines at V5 and V6. The rock is monzogranite. Easy to combine with a visit to the Manx circuit, since you simply walk up toward Manx from Hidden Valley and look to the left for the little rockpile. A quirky stop rather than a destination of its own.

ca_gangsta_wall.blurb: An orange, slabby section of Billy Land, the dome-like formation near Echo Lakes off Echo Summit in the Lake Tahoe region, at around 7,600 feet. All ten climbs are trad, mostly between 5.6 and 5.8, plus a few harder lines up to 5.11. Expect cracks and ledges on granodiorite rather than steep face climbing. Reaching the base means pushing through some brush and a bit of third-class scrambling, after following the Pacific Crest Trail toward the 5.12 Wall. A modest, moderate-oriented wall suited to climbers comfortable placing their own gear.

ca_mel_s_diner_boulder.blurb: A friendly boulder in the Lost Horse bouldering area of Joshua Tree National Park, a short flat stroll from the start of Lost Horse Road. Ten problems, mostly very easy to V0 with one harder line around V4, on granodiorite with plenty of jugs at a manageable height. It stays mostly shady, which helps on warm days. Great for beginners, families or a quick warm-up and cool-down; some of the easiest problems can be done without a pad. Experienced boulderers will want to head on to the larger circuits nearby.

ca_jimmy_cliff_boulder.blurb: A large boulder at the foot of the Jimmy Cliff formation in the Lost Horse area of Joshua Tree National Park. Ten problems, with the bulk at the easy end (very easy through V1), a handful in the middle and a harder line around V4. It sits within the wider Jimmy Cliff boulder field, so it pairs well with neighbouring blocks. The walk in is around 15 to 20 minutes from the car on easy ground, from either the Lost Horse Road end or the Real Hidden Valley lot. Bring a pad or two; it is a good stop for mixed-ability groups.
